description.narrative: The ongoing conflict has posed numerous challenges for both the refugees and the host communities in Sudan. The conflict in the country has been a major catalyst for the displacement of countless individuals, forcing them to seek refuge in relatively safer states, putting strain on already limited resources, infrastructure and social services. The objective of the CPO SDN102 is enhancing skills acquisition, particularly in rural and agricultural livelihoods, to support forcibly displaced individuals and host communities though strengthen Vocational and Informal Apprenticeships Training Systems in Sudan The PROSPECT Partnership in Sudan (SDN/19/50/NLD funded by the Government of the Netherlands for 9,04 Mio USD) aims to achieve sustainable improvements in the wellbeing and independence of forcibly displaced persons (FDPs) and host communities (HCs) in Sudan. Under this Partnership, the International Labour Organization (ILO), the International Finance Corporation (IFC), the United Nations Children’s Fund, and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), have developed complementary interventions in the states of White Nile and Kassala States. Under PROSPECTS, the ILO works under the Pillar 1 programming stream to support the integration of refugees, IDPs, and returnees into relevant learning and skills development interventions. Remote and deep field project locations require innovative programming, institutional capacity building, facility and instructional revitalization, and targeted investments to build up the capacity to provide skills trainings to rural and agricultural dependent household members. A range of assessments and appraisals have guided programme activity design and development. Proposed intervention aims brand skills development and TVET and to enhance the meaningful participation and engagement of young people, especially girls, in addressing the specific barriers to skilling and employment.
